articles.title: Insomniac Clears the Air After Marvel's Wolverine Fans Confuse Lady Deathstrike for Psylocke
articles.summary: Insomniac Games has cleared the air after a new trailer for Marvel's Wolverine had fans confusing Lady Deathstrike for Psylocke.
articles.body:
Insomniac Games has cleared the air after a new trailer for Marvel's Wolverine had fans confusing Lady Deathstrike for Psylocke.

If you thought the launch trailer for the PlayStation 5-exclusive video game would come and go without controversy, I've got bad news. Despite coming in at a little less than a minute and a half long, Marvel's Wolverine managed to kick up a storm of confusion online after fans spotted what they believed was a new character wielding a familiar-looking purple energy sword.

In comments across YouTube, Instagram, X/Twitter, and other social media platforms, you don't have to look too hard to find watchers questioning if the sneering villain featured in the launch trailer was Psylocke. Psylocke is an energy-wielding mutant who's been known to show up across various X-Men stories in the past, so when a glowing sword showed up in Marvel's Wolverine, many believed it to be a grand character reveal.

Well, it's not, and Insomniac has done its best to make that clear.

Deathstrike. #WolverinePS5 pic.twitter.com/koWhS5v3HG — Insomniac Games (@insomniacgames) September 5, 2026

The post above was published earlier today and labels the sword user as Lady Deathstrike. The PlayStation developer didn't outright say it's trying to quiet the noise that's emerged in the days following the trailer's reveal, but judging by the comments, many are shocked any clarification was needed in the first place.

"The fact it has to be stated is so crazy to me," one user said . "Larp monsters are everywhere."

"No that’s Psylocke, some guy told me and he’s for sure right," another user joked .

It really does seem to be the purple sword that's to blame here because, as some have noted, Lady Deathstrike looks nothing like Psylocke. The version of the character featured in Marvel's Wolverine doesn't exactly have a comic-accurate design, but her vest and hair do more to link her to Lady Deathstrike than the character many were making her out to be.

There's also the fact that Insomniac has talked about Lady Deathstrike being in Marvel's Wolverine before, with the launch trailer also being far from the first time we've even seen her in the game. For example, one early look at her new design arrived in July's Ain't No Hero trailer , while a GIF the studio posted on social media showed her looking down on viewers.

These aren't clips of her doing anything you'd expect Psylocke to do either. This version has been shown attacking Logan with Lady Deathstrike's instantly recognizable finger claws on full display multiple times. Why she's using that sword or where it came from remains a mystery, but whatever the reason, it's not because she's actually Psylocke. That's not to say that character isn't in the game at all; other X-Men regulars like Jean Grey and Sabretooth are confirmed to make an apperance. If Psylockie is in the game, though, Insomniac hasn't publicly said a thing about her.

Logan will at least take on Lady Deathstrike – not Psylocke – when Marvel's Wolverine launches for PS5 September 15, 2026. Meanwhile, the launch trailer actually arrived as part of a recent State of Play presentation from Sony, which you can catch up on here . For more, you can check out IGN's last full preview and our breakdown for the game's many, many suits .

articles.title: Left 4 Dead 2 Dev Admits Valve Intentionally Leaked Its Own Trailer After the ESRB Blocked It from Release
articles.summary: Former Valve writer Chet Faliszek has a confession to make: Valve intentionally leaked its own Left 4 Dead 2 trailer.
articles.body:
Former Valve writer Chet Faliszek has a confession to make: Valve intentionally leaked its own Left 4 Dead 2 trailer.

The Half-Life and Portal veteran spilled the beans on the studio's past unconventional marketing tactics in a new video uploaded to his YouTube channel (via Ars Technica ). Based on his recounting of the Left 4 Dead 2 incident, Valve "leaked our trailer ahead of time because" the Entertainment Software Rating Board (ESRB) "wouldn't let us release the trailer."

So, why are we just hearing about this now? Well, it's been a few years since any of this would have mattered.

"I think we can't get in trouble for that now. It was like 20 years ago," Faliszek said. "It's funny seeing leaked stuff now because, yeah, I don't think you can look for 'leaked Left 4 Dead 2 trailer' because it's just going to be lost."

Leaks can happen for a variety of reasons. Sometimes companies are hacked and have their content spilled out onto the internet ; sometimes someone says something they shouldn't , and sometimes materials are mistakenly published early . Most developers and publishers have their own process to ensure leaks don't happen, but in the case of Left 4 Dead 2, Valve saw opportunity.

The leaked footage in question appears to be the Zombie Survival Guide cinematic trailer , which maybe not-so-mysteriously appeared online in October 2009, one month before the launch of Left 4 Dead 2. It's a three-minute story video that lets survivors Coach, Ellis, Nick, and Rochelle loose to tear through hordes of zombies with chainsaws, guns, and more. Although it's quite violent, Faliszek didn't say exactly what the ESRB had taken issue with. Whatever it was, it didn't seem to matter much to Valve.

"Yeah, it originally got leaked because we had this with the ESRB, so that's why a lot of the language had to get toned down," he continued.

It all certainly seemed to work out for the best – at least for Valve. Left 4 Dead 2 went on to launch to rave reviews from critics and fans, including a 9/10 review from IGN. Although it never led to a third game (because of course it didn't), we found a lot to love about the multiplayer zombie sequel, calling it "one of the most distinctive co-operative titles out there" at the time.

For more on Valve, you can check out our list of the top 10 best games the studio has made . You can also learn about the recent leak that has fans digging through more than a decade of files .

articles.title: How to Watch the September 2026 Nintendo Direct and Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct
articles.summary: Nintendo is going big this September with two Nintendo Direct showcases airing on back-to-back days. Here's everything you need to know.
articles.body:
People are always asking, “When is the next Nintendo Direct??” And for the next few days, the appropriate answer is, “Which one?” That’s because Nintendo is going big this September with two Nintendo Direct showcases airing on back-to-back days . Outside of game-specific presentations like the Splatoon Raiders and Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave Directs, these will be the first Nintendo Directs since the big June 2026 showcase that gave us our first glimpse at The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake . We’re expecting to see a lot more of that on Tuesday, as the first show is The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct, followed by a general Nintendo Direct and a Nintendo Treehouse: Live stream on Wednesday.

IGN will host live watch parties for each presentation; here’s everything you need to know about how to watch the September 2026 Nintendo Directs.

When Does the Zelda 40th Anniversary Nintendo Direct Start?

Nintendo is getting things started with The Legend of Zelda on Tuesday, September 8, at 7am PT / 10am ET / 4pm CEST . Nintendo said that the livestream will last roughly 30 minutes, adding, “To celebrate the series’ 40th anniversary, we will deliver a variety of information related to The Legend of Zelda.”

IGN will host a pre-show five minutes before the Direct , starting at 6:55am PT / 9:55am ET / 3:55 pm CEST.

Once the Direct ends, stick around for a live Nintendo Voice Chat post-show featuring Zelda experts and superfans Logan Plant (that’s me!), Brian Altano, and Peer Schneider – who reviewed the original Ocarina of Time back in 1998, you know. They’ll talk for an hour about everything covered in the show.

We’ll also liveblog the Direct as it airs with everything that happens, and cover all of the important news right here on IGN.

When Does the September 2026 Nintendo Direct Start?

The day after Zelda’s birthday bash, Nintendo will stream a second Direct. It will air Wednesday, September 9, at 7am PT / 10am ET / 4pm CEST. This is the more general Nintendo Direct, focusing on, “Nintendo Switch 2 games launching this winter.” But don’t worry, Nintendo’s press releases always use that short-term language, and you can generally bank on a couple of announcements that will go beyond that limited timeframe.

IGN will yet again host a pre-show five minutes before the Direct , starting at 6:55am PT / 9:55am ET / 3:55 pm CEST.

Stick around after the watch party for another Nintendo Voice Chat post-show where we’ll spend an hour breaking down everything that happened in the Nintendo Direct.

How to Watch the September 2026 Nintendo Directs

Both of IGN’s watch parties will be right here on IGN, and across our social channels:

What to Expect From the September 2026 Nintendo Direct and Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct

As usual, Nintendo is keeping its announcements close to the chest before the Directs. But that doesn’t mean we can’t make some reasonable guesses! Starting with Zelda, we’ll almost certainly get our first big look at the Ocarina of Time remake as well as its release date, as it’s slated to come out this year. I’m also expecting a formal reveal of The Legend of Zelda movie, due out next April. It could be more casting news, or a short clip from the film. I’m also hoping we’ll get Twilight Princess added to Switch Online, as it’s currently the only 3D Zelda game not playable on Switch 2 in some way.

In the general Direct, I’m expecting updates on the rest of Nintendo’s 2026 slate, which includes Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave, Nintendo Switch Sports Resort, and hopefully The Duskbloods, which has been set for 2026 but hasn’t gotten an official date yet. We’ll also probably get a look at Xenoblade Genesis, the next entry in Monolith Soft’s RPG series due in 2027. Beyond that, it’s anyone’s guess.

And I took quite a few guesses. For more fun speculation, check out 14 predictions for the Nintendo Direct and Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct . I think it’s going to be a very, very fun week.

Logan Plant is the host of Nintendo Voice Chat and IGN's Senior Editor, Playlist and DB. The Legend of Zelda is his favorite video game franchise of all time, and he is patiently awaiting the day Nintendo announces a brand new F-Zero. You can find new episodes of NVC every Friday on the IGN Games YouTube channel, Apple Podcasts, Spotify, or your favorite podcast app.

articles.title: We Tested the Skytech Gaming Blaze 5: Is This Mid-Tier Gaming PC With an RTX 5070 Worth Your Money Despite a Few Annoying Design Flaws?
articles.summary: The Skytech Gaming Blaze 5 is packed with strong mid-tier components in a sleek glassy tower, but there are a few issues that’ll impact your quality of life.
articles.body:
A custom pre-built gaming PC like the Skytech Gaming Blaze 5 is going to save you a lot of work if you’re not technically savvy or simply don’t have the patience to put together a modern-day puzzle. With its Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070 graphics card and AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D, you’re getting solid mid-tier performance. And it’s all packed away in an easy-to-open glass case with shiny RGB components.

Skytech Gaming Blaze 5 – Hands-on Photos

That said, it’s not without issue. Upgrading or replacing components is likely going to take moving a few things out of the way, as it’s a bit crowded on the motherboard. Even if you don’t plan on upgrading, you’ll either be annoyed by the finicky RGB lighting or the fact that the power button and front ports are at the very bottom of the tower, making floor placement very awkward. These may not be dealbreakers for some, but you should know what you’re getting into.

Skytech Gaming Blaze 5 – Case Design and Build Layout

The Skytech Gaming Blaze 5 isn’t terribly bigger than your average mid-tower, coming in at 18.3 x 20.6 x 9.4 inches. A good chunk of the sides are wrapped in tempered glass and RGB LEDs, with light bars found around the case, on the seven case fans, the two RAM sticks, and the PSU shroud – the GPU is the only component left out of the fun. The rest of the case is painted black, which isn’t my favorite gamer aesthetic, but it does allow the rest of the RGB to shine.

Breaking into this rig is pleasantly easy. The glass panel pops off with a little pressure, held in by several pegs and a larger clip. The RTX 5070 isn’t terribly large, but it doesn’t leave a lot of headroom for one of the two PCIe 4.0 x16 slots that are available just beneath it. If you did want to plug something in there, it’d need to be relatively thin, and I’d worry about how tight it would be squeezed up against the GPU. All the cables are neatly tucked away, but you’ll need to work around a few things to replace some components. For example, the CPU fan cables are blocking the RAM and the SSD sits very snugly between the CPU and the motherboard’s heatsink.

Popping open the panel on the opposite side was just as easy, held in place by the same mechanism. All the cables are zip tied and lined up cleanly on the front, but of course, there’s a mess of wires down by the 850W Gold PSU. The PSU is non-modular, too, so if you need to replace a cable, you’re going to have to buy a new PSU and play connect the dots.

The front glass panel pops off easily from the top and slots back in just as smoothly. You’ll find the front connectors just below the glass panel, near the power button. There’s a headphone jack as well as two USB 2 Type-A and one USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-C slot. The placement for the power button as well as the ports is mighty annoying if the PC is placed on the floor as opposed to your desk.

On the back, you’ll find two USB 3.2 Gen 1 Type-A, one USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-A, five USB 2 Type-A, one USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-C, an RJ-45 Ethernet, and three audio ports. There are also connectors for Wi-Fi 6 extenders as well as an HDMI and DisplayPort on the motherboard, which are helpful for troubleshooting. There was a sticker on the back blocking the ports and pulling it off left a sticky residue in places, which is very silly, but you’ll need to clean it up.

Fortunately, there’s no real bloatware clogging up the metaphorical pores of the Skytech Gaming Blaze 5. However, it does come packaged with the SignalRGB app, which is a slightly annoying app that gives you access to the system’s RGB lighting settings as well as control over your fans and the ability to monitor hardware performance. You do have to customize the monitoring interface yourself. And it asks you to create an account to get access to more lighting features. And then it asks you to sign up for a Pro account ($6 per month) to remove the ads. Yes, there are ads in your RGB lighting configuration app. Like I said, it is an annoying app to deal with.

I also noticed some issues with the RGB lighting overall. There’s no direct setting to turn off the RGB – only to pause or dim the effect, both of which do disable the lighting. However, the lighting will occasionally flicker back on and then off again. And when starting the PC, the app doesn’t remember that you disabled the lighting so it’ll kick back on. Another issue I noticed is that the RGB lighting occasionally stutters when active, like it’s skipping a beat.

The Skytech Gaming Blaze 5 features an Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070 12GB GPU, AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D, and 32GB of RAM, which will get you mid-tier gaming performance. Unfortunately, it doesn’t feel like mid-tier pricing (at $2,299), but perhaps that’s to be expected given the current computing climate . Overall, you can get roughly 50 to 60 fps in select AAA games at 4K on high settings. And of course, Nvidia’s DLSS frame generation will get you further to capitalize on high refresh rate displays.

Taking a tour through Night City in Cyberpunk 2077, the Skytech Gaming Blaze 5 averaged 60 fps at 4K on the Ray Tracing Ultra and DLSS Performance settings. It achieves greater heights with frame generation (x2), scoring 97 fps, and then 167 fps with frame generation (x4). Unfortunately, the RTX 5070 can’t reach the full potential of super high refresh rate panels, like 240Hz.

With simple DLSS Performance, the Blaze 5 managed 56 fps in Assassin’s Creed Shadows and 78 fps with frame generation enabled. Naturally, the Blaze 5 fell low on the Metro Exodus benchmark, at 40 fps, since it’s a heavier workload with no upscaling. In a more competitive game, like Black Ops 7, it operated smoothly at 121 fps, which is more than enough to get you up on those leaderboards.

Pragmata is a little intense to run on an RTX 5070 at 4K, max settings without any additional help. I started scouring space-dystopian New York City in the space-daddy simulator, and I averaged 40 fps on the highest settings with DLSS Performance enabled. Then I turned on frame generation (x4) and fought the freaky baby-looking robots that haunt my nightmares, which got me around 124 fps. Meanwhile, at 1440p with no frame generation, the Blaze 5 scored 71 fps.

You can definitely get by when gaming at 4K, but the Blaze 5 will really shine with a 1440p monitor, capturing those higher frames you want to see. It does cost a hefty sum, so you might as well optimize accordingly.

Rami Tabari is a contributing writer at IGN with over 9 years of experience in the tech and gaming industry. You can find his bylines at Laptop Mag and Tom's Guide (and on a random Predator review at Space.com). When Rami isn't wading through a sea of the latest gaming tech, he's agonizing over the worldbuilding in his upcoming novella.

articles.title: Hot Wheels Infinite Rush Review, Gameplay Impressions, Videos and Top Features
articles.summary: Hot Wheels Infinite Rush from developer Milestone aims to strike a balance between faithfully recreating the beloved toy line in all its glory while also competing with the best arcade racers on the market.
articles.body:
Hot Wheels Infinite Rush from developer Milestone aims to strike a balance between faithfully recreating the beloved toy line in all its glory while also competing with the best arcade racers on the market.

The follow-up to Hot Wheels Unleashed 2: Turbocharged from 2023, Infinite Rush expands in big ways, smoothly pushing a staggering number of vehicles into specific types and letting them loose over sprawling open-world environments with an almost intimidating number of things to do.

Quietly a powerhouse series that boasts great arcade-racing bones, Infinite Rush might just be the entry that breaks it out of the niche and into something much bigger.

Infinite Rush is a, well, rush for anyone who enjoyed the toy vehicles since the late '60s.

Granted, everything looks good with the modern graphical horsepower driving the experience. It wouldn't be a quality racing game without the stars of the show looking great. It's almost a little eyebrow-raising at how much these on-screen toys look like the real thing, be it the attention to detail, the way they move, the decals, etc.

But the game goes beyond that, making sure that, over the course of four islands, it matches the heavyweight names of the genre in scope while also managing to feel like, frankly, a cared-for playset in a kid's room.

Wheelswood is the expected cityscape with huge skyscrapers, floating blimps and the like. Tentacle Bay is a more nature-based romp that lives up to its name. Gearville is all about heavy machinery out in the desert. Drifty Temples goes a little cyberpunk with neon lights, cherry trees and temples, to name a few of the landmarks.

In all, it's a brilliant backdrop with a rather stunning attention to detail, too. It's loads of fun when the world plays with perspective, too, flipping players up into the sky on a track that has them looking below at the vast lands sweeping by at high speeds.

At launch, there are four vehicle types:

Even younger audiences won't need much help with the types. Versatile is balanced. Titan, all power. Speeder gets bonus boost charge. Drifter can breeze through corners at high speed.

It's all in the name of earning that boost, of course. Each type earns boost in different ways, and those who can navigate the courses and the game-within-a-game that is boost management will win the races or top the challenges chart.

Players will take these through different game modes, including waypoint races, time attacks, elimination sprints and even a drift mode.

After Mario Kart mastered it, a free roam feels like a must for these types of games. It makes the cut here and offers a variety of different things to do such as seeking out stunts and collectibles, checkpoint races, photo snapping and quite a bit more.

By far the best is encountering other drivers out in the open world who want to race through traffic and whatnot. Beat them, add their car to the collection. Hunting for those out in the world is just plain fun, as is the dopamine rush of actually finding one.

It's all-ages fun, really. A kid of almost any age can pick up a controller and let the imagination go wild. But there's some notable skill-gap stuff and even depth in the creation department for the big (adult) kids who grew up with this stuff, too.

For those who want to seek out solo glory, there's a small campaign here worth a look.

Players advance the campaign through certain portals that hold specific events. These loop in the different vehicle types and game modes and beating them progresses things.

The end goal won't shock: Players will advance through each island by defeating "rush squads" and eventually the "rush master" at their own game.

Granted, there isn't some must-see story here or a deep dive on a create-a-character thing that Lego brands could probably explore better. But there's so much going on in these four maps and things are so consistently varied that it's hard to complain. Same story for the expected perk system that lets players sprinkle a little of their own preferences onto the rides.

There's a pretty solid, modern-feeling bit of online love going on here too. There are ranked lobbies and chill playlist modes with voting enabled for what comes next.

This online idea extends to customization, a must for a Hot Wheels game. Players can tweak fun things about their ride like boost sounds, a livery editor and even a track builder.

This is where a big bit of replayability comes from, as players can then engage with other players' track creations in the world. It's going to be a treat to see what some of the more creative elements in the scene come up with, keeping things fresh.

There's already post-launch support mapped out, too, which will keep flushing new rides into the experience. And as a whole the game runs well and comes with the expected options in the menus, too.

Like Lego 2K Drive before it, Infinite Rush is not just a lazy IP effort content to do the usual stuff and call it a day.

Rather, Infinite Rush is a love letter to the toys themselves that will appeal to all ages, really. Perhaps most impressively, it's quietly and simply one of the better arcade racers on the market outright.

While some series are bogged down in sliders and assists and dedicated parts analysis in million-dollar garage simulations, Infinite Rush hammers nostalgia and sheer fun buttons on repeat, impressively leaning into depth and online replayability that will keep it around with happy players for a long, long time.

articles.title: Riot Co-Founder Calls League of Legends MMO the 'Grail' Quest, 5 Years After It Was Announced
articles.summary: League of Legends developer Riot Games is still bashing away on its MMO, which co-founder Mark Merrill recently described as the studio’s "grail quest."
articles.body:
League of Legends developer Riot Games is still bashing away on its MMO, which co-founder Mark Merrill recently described as the studio’s “grail quest.”

Riot announced its MMO five years ago , in August 2021. Since then it’s seen a number of changes and various high-profile developers exit the project. But speaking to Kinda Funny Games’ Greg Miller at PAX , Merrill insisted it’s still in the works.

“We know what players’ hopes and dreams are,” he said. “It’s just on us as a team, and can we succeed in the execution?”

Merrill said Riot jokingly calls the MMO the “grail” because “f**k it, many a brave knight are gonna die on the grail quest. But f**k it, it’s the grail, so let’s go.”

“That’s the mindset that we really try to cultivate. And that is hard to do at scale,” he continued. “But I think we’re doing a reasonable job. And I think the future’s incredibly bright.”

It’s fair to say Merrill’s comments were met with a healthy dose of skepticism, particularly from fighting game fans. Riot recently announced its League of Legends fighting game, 2XKO, ends active development at the end of this year due to a lack of players. It only released late 2025, so you can understand where this sentiment is coming from.

“They hyping up this MMO like they aren’t just going to shoot it in the face after six months cause it won’t be bigger than WoW,” commented X / Twitter user and fighting game community member sl0th .

“It’s gonna release at the same time as a FF14 expansion for some reason and they’ll kill it in three months because it didnt make a f***youillion dollars,” added Shinhua .

“Why would anyone be excited for anything they release when they fumbled 2XKO as hard as they did.” commented Gil . “No faith they can handle a MMO when that's 2x harder to please people.”

League of Legends 2025 Cinematic Trailer: New Character Designs

Will the League MMO actually come out? In January, former World of Warcraft producer Raymond Bartos joined Riot Games, giving fans renewed hope that the project will eventually see the light of day . The appointment came after the MMO was “reset” back in 2024 , with Merrill stating at the time that Riot had gone back to the drawing board “some time ago.”

Concern grew in 2022 when then-executive producer Greg Street warned fans that there was “no guarantee” the League MMO would ship. The lead then went on to announce his departure from Riot in early 2023 .

Two years ago, when he announced the development reset, Merrill said he understood fans' frustration at the lack of progress on the MMO, but insisted the time spent in the dark would “help provide space for the team to focus on the incredible amount of work ahead of them.”

“Remember, 'no news is good news,' as it means we're hard at work, pouring our hearts and souls into making something that we hope you’ll love," he continued.

articles.title: Competitive Pokémon is on phones now, but you still need a Switch to become a champion
articles.summary: The mobile version of Pokémon Champions isn’t allowed at high-level tournaments, but it’s unclear why.
articles.body: To get started with competitive Pokémon battles, all you need is your phone. But to compete at the highest level, like at the Pokémon World Championships, you’re going to need a Switch. And there doesn’t seem to be a good reason why. Battle simulator Pokémon Champions originally launched on the Switch and Switch 2 in April, with the mobile version following in June. The experience is nearly identical across the game’s versions; since it’s cross-platform, the choice really comes down to what devices you own and whether you prefer tapping or using a controller. I find myself playing Champions on my phone more often just because it’s always in my pocket and I’m blessed with unlimited data. But at this year’s World Championships, the mobile version of Champions wasn’t allowed in competition. As of September 1st, certain local tournaments will allow the mobile version, but regional-level tournaments and above will still require Switch hardware to compete. During a roundtable interview at Worlds last week — before the September 1st rules refresh — Champions producer Masaaki Hoshino addressed its absence from the competition. “The reason why we’re using Switch right now is just because graphics are quite nice on the Switch 2,” he said via an interpreter. “Also, because [with] mobile there’s just so many devices out there, if we allow people to bring their own devices, it can be a bit complicated from that perspective.” This answer made less sense before the rules were updated. Tournaments at the regional level and higher are streamed on official channels, and VGC — the name for the competitive video game circuit — was the most viewed of the four games featured at Worlds this year, according to Esports Charts. Based on Hoshino’s answer and the new rules, it seems like The Pokémon Company views mobile as fine for smaller tournaments, but maybe not premium enough for the biggest VGC stages. (The Worlds finals took place in the Chase Center in San Francisco this year, only the second time the finals have ever been held in an arena as opposed to a hotel ballroom or convention center hall. Production values and attendance were especially high.) [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: Champions is certainly sharper on Switch 2 than on my iPhone 14 Pro, and it makes sense to want to present the best version of the flagship VGC game in a series often criticized for its graphics. But while competitors are required to bring their own devices to tournaments, the official VGC rules handbook does call out one case where hardware might be provided: during streamed matches. Players can generate a “team ID” for the battle team they’re using in a tournament, and technically anyone can use that ID to create a “replica” of that team on their own account. The handbook says specifically that “Team IDs may be used for recordkeeping or team checks, and they may be utilized on hardware provided by the Tournament Organizer for streamed matches.” If visual fidelity is a concern, there’s at least a workaround already available. But is there a technical reason not to allow mobile at every level of competition? “Given that Champions is available on both mobile and Switch, cross-platform play is the trickiest thing,” Hoshino said. “All of the battle calculation is done on the server side, so this is what enables the cross-platform play, but it also was one of the trickiest things in developing Champions.” So in short, not really. The trickiness of cross-platform play possibly explains the gap between the console and mobile releases of Champions, but that’s solved now that both versions are out (barring things like regular server maintenance, I suppose). Mobile is also not a problem for other competitive Pokémon games. The mobile version of Pokémon Unite is allowed in high-level competition and it’s worked just fine, though only one player in the finals this year appeared to be playing on a phone as opposed to a Switch. Pokémon Go is only on mobile, and its competitive matches are streamed just like the VGC ones are. These aren’t the best examples in favor of mobile — this was Unite’s last year in the World Championships, and the Pokémon Go spectator experience is by far the worst of the bunch for several reasons — but it’s clearly possible to make mobile work. Hoshino said that across the Switch 2 and mobile combined, Pokémon Champions has been downloaded around 25 million times. Given that number is higher than the total Switch 2 install base as of June, it’s likely that at least a few million of those downloads were on mobile devices. It’s anyone’s guess how many of those players are exclusively playing on mobile, but with the recent Switch 2 price hike and higher tech prices overall, it’s possible that at least some prospective Champions competitors will own a phone but not have the budget for a Switch. Building a team and prepping for a tournament is the same whether you’re playing Champions on Switch or your phone. With the single exception of Eternal Flower Floette, which is only obtainable through Pokémon Legends: Z-A, you can get every pokémon you might need for a team within Champions using the gacha-style “recruit” feature. It’s quicker and easier if you already own some Switch Pokémon games, since you can transfer pokémon you caught from those games into Champions via the cloud storage service Pokémon Home, but it’s possible to get the pokémon you need without spending any money on Champions. It’s also easier than ever to train those pokémon and get them battle-ready; what used to take hours in-game now only takes a few minutes. [Image: [Image: So it’s not like mobile-only players — or those who’ve only played Champions in general — are majorly disadvantaged in teambuilding. (That said, Eternal Floette was on the winning team this year and many other competitors’ teams besides, and players have criticized it for being a “pay-to-win” pokémon.) If you don’t have a Switch for whatever reason, you could absolutely start your championship run on mobile and potentially qualify for Worlds — and then not have the hardware needed to compete there. Locking those players out of high-level competition feels like a mistake when the stated ethos of Pokémon Champions is “to be inclusive and accessible to all players.” That’s evident in the game’s design, which makes previously obfuscated information easy to access and understand, and it’s clear from the viewership of this year’s World Championships — in addition to the thousands of spectators in attendance at the arena — that VGC is growing. When I attended the Pokémon World Championships in 2016, the last time they were in San Francisco, it was a niche event held in a hotel; now the official MLB account is posting references to the championship-winning VGC play. I’ve been playing and following VGC for a long time, and it’s a rich, deep game with a passionate and largely welcoming community — I’m thrilled to see it getting more popular and accessible. It just makes sense to keep tournaments as accessible as possible, too.

articles.title: Exodus Ending and Character Fates Change Based on Your Choices
articles.summary: Exodus is an upcoming sci-fi RPG that will account for the decisions you make in its story, and its narrative director explains how it'll all be reflected in the end.
articles.body:
Any time you look at or talk about Exodus, the upcoming space opera RPG from Archetype Entertainment, the Mass Effect comparisons start flying at light speed. I mean, Exodus narrative director Drew Karpyshyn played a major role as a writer and lead at BioWare to shape the stories of its biggest hits. In our conversation following my hands-on preview of Exodus , he told me that Mass Effect is a perfectly fine way for people to wrap their head around what this new game is.

The parallels don't end with the Paladin/Immortal morality system or the romance and relationship dynamics that are going to drive the story, either. He hinted at how the decisions you make can impact Exodus' ending. Of course, that's not exclusive to BioWare games by any stretch, but when the Mass Effect 2's suicide mission is regarded as a series pinnacle, no one would blame to draw a quick comparison.

When I asked about the relationship systems in Exodus, Karpyshyn emphasized wanting to make them feel real and said it's about, "[M]aking their relationship with you grow, allowing it to evolve from the choices you've made, and realizing that the choices you make are going to bring some companions closer to you, but maybe push some companions farther away."

He took it one step further, and told me, "Without spoiling too much, we definitely want to have it impact how their storylines go." Then he took it another step further and concluded, "Depending on choices you make, by the end of the game, you might not have every companion with you that you started with. That's about all I can say!"

Those are aspects of an RPG in this style that I would've bet on being included, but it's nice to get confirmation that Exodus is following suit. However, from our conversation it may not seem like it's entirely due to characters facing life-or-death situations. He talked at length about companions butting heads with you and being conflicted about what you say and the actions you take in key moments.

He expanded on how other in-game events can factor into how the story unfolds, saying, "Even within that optional content, there are choices that will lock or unlock certain things, change the way things play out, change relationships, change characters, change… future… missions…" Hmm, smells like loyalty missions to me!

Perhaps companions can reach a breaking point and leave the party entirely. And maybe their affinity toward you or the situations they face throughout the story will impact their survival in the end.

We'll know for sure when Exodus launches on April 7, 2027 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC. For more on the upcoming sci-fi RPG, be sure to check out my hands-on preview for Exodus and read my full interview with Drew Karpyshyn .

Michael Higham is an editor at IGN who regularly contributes with reviews, previews, features, and news in written and video form. He's usually entrusted with covering long RPGs and tech products, but he's got range when it comes to games. You'll also catch him at events and hosting video content, including IGN's weekly podcast Unlocked .

articles.title: Lanterns Episode 4 Wastes Two Major DC Villains, but the Series' Fundamental Appeal Is Still There
articles.summary: Lanterns stumbles a bit in Episode 4 as it fails to take full advantage of some key DC characters, but the series’ core strengths remain. Read our full review.
articles.body:
Warning: This review contains full spoilers for Lanterns Season 1, Episode 4!

Lanterns sure left us hanging these past couple of weeks, ending Episode 2 with the debut of Ulrich Thomsen’s Sinestro and then pivoting away to tell a flashback storyline in Episode 3 ( a great flashback storyline , but a flashback all the same). Only now in Episode 4 do we see the full reunion between Sinestro and his former protege. It’s a definite high point of the episode, albeit an all too brief one.

It’s slightly ironic that a show about Manhunters is taking some inspiration from 1986’s Manhunter (and its literary inspiration, Thomas Harris’ Red Dragon). Sinestro is clearly being cast as the Hannibal Lecter figure in this particular investigation, providing his former protege with some much-needed advice and also taking the opportunity to screw with him psychologically. Thomsen really shines in this opening scene. He conveys a clear menace, but you also get a real sense of the history and camaraderie between Sinestro and Kyle Chandler’s Hal. As readers of Geoff Johns’ seminal Green Lantern run will know well, Sinestro ultimately sees himself as nothing more or less than Hal’s friend. He may have ulterior motives in this show, but he seems to be genuinely trying to help Hal out of a dangerous predicament.

My main complaint here, again, is that the Hal/Sinestro reunion is over too soon. Sinestro is too key a character to the Green Lantern mythos to be treated as such a small supporting player. I would have loved more of this sci-fi-flavored spin on the classic Will Graham/Hannibal Lecter dynamic, whether that consists of flashbacks to their pre-uprising relationship or simply more scenes of the two conversing in the prison. Later on, Hal recounts what Sinestro told him about Manhunters struggling to replicate human hearts. Why couldn’t we have seen that portion of their conversation? We can only hope the series finds room to bring Thomsen back in a more substantive role in the back half of Season 1, but right now, it seems just as likely this is all we’re going to see of the character.

I feel similarly about the other key GL villain introduced in Episode 4, Jason Manuel Olazábal’s Hector Hammond. We basically get one good, solid sequence out of Hector and that’s it. The standoff between Hector and Hal/John (Aaron Pierre) is tense and stressful in the best way, but it’s also over very quickly. At that point, we learn that Hector is really just Hector Gutiérrez, another fakeout used by the Manhunter to throw our heroes off their scent. And unlike Sinestro, there’s not even any prior history between Hal and Hector in this universe. This is a major DC villain who’s being effectively wasted as a one-off misdirection.

So there’s definitely a newfound element of frustration to Lanterns in Episode 4. Up till now, I haven’t minded the series’ decision to downplay some of the franchise’s more fantastical trappings. It’s necessary from a practical TV-making perspective, and it suits the story being told. But seeing such major GL characters being introduced and then whisked off the board so unceremoniously is harder to stomach.

Fortunately, Lanterns still has its biggest selling point to fall back upon - the eternal friction between cantankerous veteran Hal Jordan and ambitious rookie John Stewart. That strength remains fully on display in Episode 4, which manages to deftly balance the inherent comedy of this pairing and the simmering tensions within Rushville. In the case of the former, we get a lot of fun banter between the two characters, and even some good jokes regarding John’s dour, stoic demeanor. Plus, there’s the heightened nature of their latest, very awkward meeting with a proudly naked Will Macon (Garret Dillahunt). Investigating Macon’s Weenie indeed.

Episode 4 is at its best when it highlights the growing friction between Hal and John. Both men are increasingly at odds with one another. Each is hiding things from the other. Moreover, each has been given clear advice to betray the other and elevate their own station. The question of whether John will backstab Hal and claim the ring hangs over every scene that follows his conversation with the Guardian Lianna (Laura Linney). We’ve seen that years of abusive parentage and single-minded training have molded John into a man who follows orders without question. Is that blind obedience what the Guardians crave, more than fearlessness? What happens when John is inevitably forced to choose between his desire for the ring and his loyalty to Hal? Does that loyalty even still exist following this episode’s dramatic final scene? A lot to ponder heading into Episode 5.

Also of note is that we seem to have our answer regarding the mystery of the undercover Manhunter. Despite the giant red herring that was Zoe’s “death” scene, she’s been revealed as Macon’s mysterious benefactor. As far as twists go, this one is pretty obvious, so it’s just as well the writers didn’t drag things out any longer. Predictable or not, it’s a reveal that works, and I’m excited to see where things go now that the Lanterns (and Antaan’s crew) know who their quarry is. We may be only halfway through the season, but the 2016 conflict sure is heating up.

One final sidebar - I didn’t really hone in on this before, but it’s certainly interesting that Sheriff Kerry (Kelly Macdonald) is a former Gotham City native whose last name is Kane. Is she somehow related to Kate Kane (and by extension, Bruce Wayne himself)? I can’t imagine the Kane/Gotham connection is mere coincidence. Presumably, we’ll get more on Kerry’s backstory before Season 1 is finished.

articles.title: Zach Cregger Says He Feels Like He's 'Running for Office' Trying to Get Skeptical Resident Evil Fans 'Not to Call Me a LARPer'
articles.summary: Resident Evil director Zach Cregger has said he feels like he’s been on an “apology tour” while navigating skepticism from some fans about his movie adaptation of Capcom’s horror franchise.
articles.body:
Resident Evil director Zach Cregger has said he feels like he’s been on an “apology tour” while navigating skepticism from some fans about his movie adaptation of Capcom’s horror franchise.

Cregger, director of hugely popular horror movies Barbarian and Weapons, has faced scrutiny from Resident Evil fans ever since it was confirmed that his adaptation wouldn’t feature any characters from the video games, or tell any of the stories already told in the video games. Instead, Cregger has charted his own path, telling a horror story set in the world of Resident Evil that references some of the video games' tropes .

In an interview with The Playlist , Cregger outlined how it has felt to promote Resident Evil amid this backlash.

Upcoming New Video Game Movies and TV Shows: 2026 Release Dates and Beyond

“I feel like I’ve been on somewhat of an apology tour,” he said. “I feel like I’m running for office, trying to get these people not to call me a LARPer.”

His comments here echo those he made to IGN’s Tom Jorgensen recently when talking about the reception to Resident Evil. “I think I was naive,” he said. “I thought fans of these games, like me, would be thrilled that somebody was coming along and turning Resident Evil into a survival horror movie. I was like, ‘That’s great.’ I did not really appreciate the sentiment that, ‘We’ve been waiting forever for Leon’s story.’ And I appreciate that, and I’m sorry that’s not the story I’m bringing. I get it, I understand the frustration. I understand it so well because I haven’t seen the earlier [Resident Evil] movies, because they don't look like the Resident Evil that I love, so how could I be frustrated with fans who have that same attitude?”

With Resident Evil now just a week away, Cregger is philosophical about fan attitude to the film. “Now, I’m just like, ‘You know what? See the movie.’” he told The Playlist. “If you still feel the same way after you’ve seen it, then whatever you think is fair. You’re going to decide if I’m an actual Resident Evil fan or a fake. What can I say? I think the movie is going to speak for itself.”

Again, those comments echo those he gave to IGN. “My only hope is that they’ll see the movie regardless of their skepticism or their disappointment that I’m not telling some of the stories that the games tell so well, and they will feel seen when they do watch the movie, and they will recognize all of the love for the games that are in this movie, because it is there,” he said.

“This is not me just telling a story and slapping Resident Evil on it so I can get a budget. This is me telling a Resident Evil story. I understand the resistance, I do, because I have it myself. It is coming from a true place of love.”

Will he get the chance to make another Resident Evil? According to Deadline , Resident Evil is tracking to make $35 million at the domestic box office during its opening weekend, although it could go higher. $35 million would be the biggest domestic opening ever in the Resident Evil franchise, beating the $26.6 million Resident Evil: Afterlife opened with in 2010.

articles.title: The Batman Part 2 Goes in 'Another Totally Different Direction,' Robert Pattinson Teases
articles.summary: Robert Pattinson has suggested The Batman Part 2 will be a very different take on the DC superhero than we’ve seen before.
articles.body:
Robert Pattinson has suggested The Batman Part 2 will be a very different take on the DC superhero than we’ve seen before.

Pattinson is set to reprise his role as the Caped Crusader in The Batman Part 2, which has a February 18, 2028 release date. Assuming it hits that date, Part 2 will arrive in theaters just shy of six years after The Batman came out.

The movie is largely shrouded in mystery, but Pattinson has started to tease what to expect from it now he’s out and about promoting his new movie, Primetime. And in an interview captured by MYmovies on TikTok , Pattinson teased something quite different than what’s gone before.

The Batman: Part II - Who's Who in Matt Reeves' DC Sequel

“Matt just wrote this amazing script,” Pattinson said of The Batman co-writer and director Matt Reeves. “I think the first one was… it’s difficult to reinvent Batman as this new thing. And then to go in another totally different direction. I’m just looking at the playback on certain things… it looks different to the first one.

“It’s just amazing. It’s a quite radical change of the script. It’s cool that Warner’s behind it, and DC. It’s just crazy. It’s a really radical retelling of Batman. I think people are going to be excited by it.”

So, what does this mean, exactly? It’s hard to tell. The Batman is a dark and gritty detective story that features a broody Bruce Wayne who struggles to stop the machinations of the Riddler. You’d imagine that Pattinson’s Batman won’t deviate too much from the version of the character we saw back in 2022, but based on what the actor’s saying here, it’s hard to predict. In truth, Pattinson is being almost comically vague about The Batman 2. Is it a courtroom drama? A psychological horror movie? A musical? Well, after Joker: Folie à Deux bombed at the box office, I doubt it’s a musical.

Perhaps The Batman 2 doubles down on the thriller aspect of its predecessor. Maybe it revolves more around its main villain, who has yet to be confirmed, than Batman. It’s unclear if Marvel star Sebastian Stan plays Harvey Dent / Two-Face , as expected, but even if he is, we’re not sure if he’s the main villain.

What we know for sure is Pattinson is finding the fight scenes in The Batman Part 2 harder than those in The Batman , now he’s in his 40s. “I’m definitely feeling my age when fighting a lot," Pattinson told GQ . "I’m literally like, ‘Goddamn, this is significantly harder than it used to be.’ But it’s really fun. And I think the movie’s going to be pretty great. It’s got a really, really fun cast, but it’s a marathon.”

It's worth remembering that Matt Reeves' The Batman movies are not a part of the ongoing DC Universe, so they're not set in the same universe as Superman, Supergirl, Lanterns, and next year's Man of Tomorrow. Reeves' The Batman and HBO spinoff show The Penguin are part of what is called The Batman Epic Crime Saga . James Gunn’s rebooted DCU will eventually see a fresh actor play Batman when The Brave and the Bold kicks into gear.

DC Universe: Every Upcoming Movie and TV Show

Speaking of The Penguin, actor Colin Farrell has said he will reprise his role as the crime boss in The Batman Part 2, although in just two scenes . Speaking to ScreenRant in June, Farrell described the script, and his involvement in the movie.

"I got to read from the first to last page and it's really magnificent,” he said. “I just think Matt Reeves is brilliant and he wrote, not only tonally, a really kind of dark and at times terrifying piece, and not only psychologically weighty and nuanced, but really feeling. It's a really... There's moments in it. It's full of feeling. I just think he wrote kind of a contemporary genre masterpiece, really. I'm only in two scenes, which is great because it means I can enjoy the rest of the film."

articles.title: Halloween: The Game Appears to Patch Out a Sex Minigame — and Players Think They Know Why
articles.summary: Halloween: The Game developer IllFonic appears to have patched out a sex mini-game after a gameplay clip went viral.
articles.body:
Halloween: The Game developer IllFonic appears to have patched out a sex minigame after a gameplay clip went viral.

The video game adaptation of the iconic 1970s slasher movie lets players have sex in a closet, but one video of this minigame featuring Samuel Loomis raised eyebrows given the character, who is in his fifties during the events of the game and is based on deceased actor Donald Pleasence’s likeness, can have sex with teenagers.

Halloween: The Game doesn’t actually launch fully until September 8, but those who bought the Halloween Deluxe Edition were able to play from this weekend, and it didn’t take long for players to notice the sex minigame.

The game includes a number of playable characters made famous by the Halloween films. Bob Simms (voiced by Nicholas Leung), Annie Brackett (voiced by Kaitlyn Robrock), Lynda van der Klok (voiced by Angela Carbone), and Laurie Strode (voiced by Chelsea Krause) are all playable civilians across single-player and multiplayer.

The character of Samuel Loomis is the main protagonist of the Halloween movies and is a “hero civilian” in the game. Loomis is the psychiatrist of series antagonist Michael Myers, and tries to prevent his patient from his murderous rampage.

In the game two players can hide in a closet. If you hide in a closet with another player already inside, you get a prompt to ask them out. If you do this and the offer is accepted, you get a button mashing minigame to raise a line on a bar as the camera shakes and the characters grunt. If both players keep the line in the right part of the bar for long enough, they'll fill up a heart and both characters get the “Stronger Together” buff. You don’t actually see the characters do anything.

LOOMIS FUCKIN LYNDA IN THE CLOSET? pic.twitter.com/NKYAyF6GYU — Monto (@TheOnlyMonto) September 4, 2026

LOOMIS FUCKIN LYNDA IN THE CLOSET? pic.twitter.com/NKYAyF6GYU

The video that went viral shows Loomis entering a closet in which 17-year-old Lynda is already hiding, then completing the sex minigame. You can imagine the Pleasance estate — if it wasn’t aware of the use of the actor’s likeness in this way before it probably is now — taking a dim view of the gameplay.

IllFonic has yet to comment (IGN has asked), but it released a hotfix this weekend hot on the heels of the game’s early access launch. The removal of the sex minigame is not mentioned in the patch notes. Here’s what IllFonic said:

The launch of Early Access for Halloween: The Game has been amazing so far and the team is so excited to finally be able to play the game with you all. Today we are rolling out our first hotfix for Halloween: The Game. This patch is primarily aimed towards addressing several crashes that have been occurring as well as a small list of other issues that the team was able to implement with this hotfix.

We are currently working on a bigger patch that addresses many issues and concerns that are being reported from the playerbase. We will continue monitoring conversations and bug reports from the community, and we greatly appreciate all your feedback. Thank you for all your love and support. See you in Haddonfield!

While IllFonic has yet to confirm the sex minigame's removal, Halloween: The Game players are now calling for it to be restored, perhaps with Samuel Loomis specifically prevented from taking part (if his inclusion is indeed the problem here). "Why did they remove it!??!?!?!?" asked redditor freetheree . "Me and my homeboy just wanna have sex in a closet? And we can’t???? Tf??????"

Some players now think they've missed out on what may go down as an early access exclusive sex minigame in Halloween: The Game.

articles.title: The Teaser for A24's Elizabeth Holmes Documentary You Can See Everything Is as Terrifying as It Is Captivating
articles.summary: A24 has released a teaser trailer for Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s surprise Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything — and it’s quite something.
articles.body:
A24 has released a teaser trailer for Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s surprise Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything — and it’s quite something.

For the uninitiated, Elizabeth Holmes is currently serving an 11-year prison sentence at the Federal Prison Camp Bryan in Texas for defrauding investors in her blood-testing startup, Theranos. Holmes, who married hotel heir Billy Evans in 2019 and with whom she has had two children (one born in 2021, the other in 2023), began her sentence on May 30, 2023.

But 34 days before she was sent to prison, Holmes invited Canadian comedian Nathan Fielder and a film crew into her home to document her every move. The film is the result of this unprecedented access and a three-year journey that certainly goes places, based on reviews to a secret screening on Sunday.

This teaser offers just a glimpse of what to expect from the 174-minute documentary, but it’s an intense watch. Fielder and Holmes are extremely close, looking into each other’s eyes as the notorious Silicon Valley founder insists she’s being genuine.

“I’m not that person,” Holmes begins as she holds Fielder’s gaze with a creepy, unwavering smile. “I can promise you that. I don’t have anything to deceive you on. Of course I’m not deceiving you. I’m engaging with you as a human being. Why would I deceive you? There’s no… there’s no reason for me to do that.”

Fielder, who wears a disbelieving expression of his own, replies: “...okay. Allright. Okay, good chat. You being real right now?”

“I’m always being real,” Holmes responds, before the camera shifts and we see that she is rocking her baby with her foot.

The scene rekindles memories of Hannibal Lecter and Clarice in Silence of the Lambs, although there isn’t a prison cell to be seen. There’s even a whiff of sexual tension in the teaser, which sets up the documentary perfectly and demands further investigation.

Filming was done in secret, and its existence was only disclosed on Sunday night via a premiere at the Telluride Film Festival. A synopsis for the film reads: “34 days before she’s sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss. From boundary-pushing directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim comes You Can See Everything . ”

According to Vanity Fair , Fielder actually lived with Holmes and her family in the days leading up to her imprisonment. He told the publication: ”I really am struggling to this day to understand exactly what I experienced.”

You Can See Everything launches in theaters in October. Holmes, meanwhile, is scheduled to be released from prison on August 16, 2032.

articles.title: 'One Season Is Perfect' — Nicolas Cage Reacts to Spider-Noir Prime Video Cancelation
articles.summary: Nicolas Cage has insisted just one season of Spider-Noir is “perfect” after Amazon canceled the Prime video show.
articles.body:
Nicolas Cage has insisted just one season of Spider-Noir is “perfect” after Amazon canceled the Prime Video show.

Spider-Noir sees Cage play Ben Reilly, a down-on-his-luck private investigator and the city's sole super-powered vigilante in 1930s New York City during the Prohibition Era. Season 1 debuted on MGM+ on May 25, 2026, followed by a global release on Prime Video two days later. You can watch Spider-Noir in both black and white, and in color.

IGN's Spider-Noir review returned an 8/10 . "Nicolas Cage’s Bogie-meets-Bugs Bunny pulp hero invigorates the highly entertaining, genre-bending Spider-Noir," we said.

Every Upcoming Spider-Man Movie Spin-Off in Development

As reported by Deadline , Spider-Noir saw a strong start in terms of viewing minutes, but it fell away soon after launch and dropped out of Prime Video’s top 10 chart. This, coupled with the high cost associated with producing the show, apparently contributed to Amazon’s decision to give it the chop.

In a statement issued to Deadline , Cage sounded philosophical about Spider-Noir coming to an end after just one season.

“For me, one season is perfect, having said what I wanted to say with this dangerous, innovative, pop-art Spider-Man,” Cage said. “Onwards, upwards, inwards.”

Spider-Noir was part of a multi-title deal between Amazon MGM Studios and Sony Pictures Television based on IP from Sony's slate of Marvel characters. Spider-Man spinoff Silk, which was part of this deal, was canceled just days after Spider-Noir was greenlit . According to Deadline, Spider-Noir’s cancelation hasn’t put an end to the deal, and multiple projects are in development.

With Spider-Man: Brand New Day breaking all sorts of box office records, our next taste of Spider-Man is Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse , which hits theaters June 18, 2027.

articles.title: PlayStation Reportedly Plotting New Killzone — but Is It a Remake or a Remaster?
articles.summary: Sony is reportedly in the early stages of bringing its first-person shooter series, Killzone, back from the dead.
articles.body:
Sony is reportedly in the early stages of bringing its first-person shooter series, Killzone, back from the dead.

Guerrilla Games’ Halo killer fell by the wayside after the developer found enormous success with Horizon Zero Dawn back in 2017. It has focused on the Horizon franchise ever since, but Killzone retains a loyal following, and fans often call for it to return.

According to MP1st , Sony may be working on doing just that, with Bulletstorm and Outriders maker People Can Fly drafted in to co-dev. But what is this new Killzone game? Apparently it’s a Killzone remaster or remake, and while we’re not sure which Killzone is getting a fresh coat of paint, the first Killzone game, released on the PlayStation 2 in 2004, is a safe bet.

The 100 Best PlayStation Games of All Time

There’s a lot going on at Guerrilla right now. PlayStation recently rebooted Horizon multiplayer spinoff Hunters Gathering following negative feedback , and, according to MP1st, the studio will move on to Killzone after it’s done doing that. According to Bloomberg , Guerrilla has until December to impress PlayStation bosses with Hunters Gathering’s next milestone, but already some Hunters Gathering staff moved over to another Guerrilla project with a milestone due at the end of this year. Apparently a “tiny team” is working on the next Horizon single-player game , which we’ll call Horizon 3 but will undoubtedly carry a new subtitle, but it’s still years away.

Perhaps a Killzone remaster or remake is a way in for PlayStation to potentially reboot the series with a brand new game at some point down the line. Either way, it’s exciting news for Killzone fans, who haven’t heard a peep out of the franchise ever since PlayStation 4 launch title Killzone Shadow Fall ( save a T-shirt in The Last of Us Part 2: Remastered ) and a Helldivers 2 crossover .

Speaking in 2024, Guerrilla Games art director Roy Postma declared the studio’s preference for the brighter, more vibrant world of Horizon over the dark and violent world of Killzone it had spent the previous decade working on.

“We were done with it as a team,” Postma said . “As a studio, we needed to refresh the palette. It was, by choice, the opposite of Killzone.”

Postma added that Horizon’s world has a wider appeal than Killzone’s: "I think the themes that this story and the characters represent are relatable for all ages and people, like having a found family of friends and finding your place in the world."

articles.title: Tarae: The Unbound Developers Hope Its East Asia Folklore Aesthetic Sets It Apart From Western Medieval Action RPGs Like Diablo
articles.summary: Tarae: The Unbound developers explain why this South Korean action RPG will stand out from the crowd.
articles.body:
One of the most impressive games I played at gamescom was Tarae: The Unbound , a new action RPG developed by South Korean studio Boundary and published by PUBG company Krafton. There’s a huge amount here that will feel familiar to fans of Diablo, not least in the way the game actually plays. But it’s how Tarae: The Unbound looks that its developers hope fans of the genre will find something unique.

Tarae: The Unbound is based in east Asia between the 15th and 17th centuries (most action RPGs, including Diablo, are set in medieval Europe), and it leans heavily on Eastern aesthetics and folklore to come up with a different take. You can see this in everything from the class design to the monsters you fight and the environments you fight them in. But the boss fights (there are over 80 at launch!) are the best example of this Eastern aesthetic — a mix of Chinese, South Korean, and Japanese influences coming together to form designs I’ve not seen in an action RPG before.

As a big fan of Diablo, I was able to settle into Tarae: The Unbound quickly, my fingers resting on the number keys for abilities, my thumb on the space bar for a dodge, and my mouse fingers clicking away to delete mobs via the weighty combat. You can even pull the camera back to get a wider view that presents almost the entire battlefield on-screen, so you can see the waves of enemies coming from a decent distance. There’s a steady stream of loot to fuss over, various skills to pick from, and, of course, build crafting.

So far, so very Diablo. But, speaking to Inyoung Koo, CEO of Boundary, art director Byung Ho Park, and creative Myung Sang Ryu in an interview following my hands-on time, I could tell that Boundary feels Tarae: The Unbound has a lot more to offer.

There are six classes in the game, each reinterpreted from Eastern cultures: the Samurai melee dealer; the Tiger Hunter (guns and traps and summon animals); Manshin , the Korean shaman who uses spiritual channeling; Geomancer (area-of-effect damage dealer); Kunoichi the ninja; and Warfiend the brawler. The campaign is made up of six acts, each of which has three or four chapters. This isn’t an open world but a linear game, so you’ll have a narrative to progress through.

“The playstyles are very different,” Boundary insisted. “So if you choose a different class you will actually feel something very different.” If you finish the campaign with one character, you don’t have to progress other classes — you can then use all the different classes in the endgame.

The developers spoke of a “balance” at play in the combat, and for me that comes mostly from the god system. There are eight different friendly or unfriendly gods who can either assist or hinder you in combat, and you’ll have to contend with these modifiers as you work your way through the campaign. Indeed, yin and yang is a common theme throughout Tarae: The Unbound; the idea that there are opposing forces at play in everything from the story to the combat.

“East Asia is where we got the inspiration from,” Boundary told me. “We wanted to take the most beautiful parts of east Asia, and we have the Buddhist cosmology as our basis — the six realms of rebirth.” There’s a human realm, an Asura realm, a beast realm, a hungry ghosts realm, and a hell realm. In the endgame, you cross the boundary of the realms to engage in battles.”

Boundary and Krafton of course face a challenge convincing western gamers to ditch their current favorite action RPG to try something new, especially considering the time investment they'll no doubt have made. But the developers are confident that they have something enticing on their hands.

“In the market, there are a lot of action RPGs, but it's mostly based in the medieval west,” Boundary said, making its pitch. “Tarae is an Eastern dark fantasy action RPG and it's got its own charms. And I talked about the combat, right? The balance in the combat is different from the existing RPGs, I believe. So I hope you can come and try.”

Boundary plans to release new content via a seasonal model, adding new characters in each season. Each year will see the release of a DLC adding a new region. “We are in this for the long haul,” Boundary said.

Tarae: The Unbound is due out on PC and consoles in 2027.

articles.title: Sentient Testicles Exist in James Gunn’s DC Universe. Don’t Act Surprised
articles.summary: Episode 4 of Lanterns confirms one of the weirder alien species we’ve ever heard of: a planet of sentient testicles.
articles.body:
Full spoilers follow for Lanterns Episode 4, “The Weenie,” including everything you need to know about the smartest testicles in the DCU!

In this week’s episode of Lanterns, there’s a funny scene where Garret Dillahunt’s William Macon disrobes in front of his captive guests, Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) and John Stewart (Aaron Pierre), so that John can draw a sketch of him. Yes, a nude sketch. While Macon retrieves John’s drawing supplies for him, an uncomfortable Hal says to his partner, “I’ve seen some shit. Even been to a planet with sentient testicles. But this is weird, right?”

Yes, Hal. It is weird. But you know, it’s not as weird as a planet with sentient testicles . You’ve been Green Lanterning for too long if you don’t realize that!

It’s nothing more than a fun moment in the episode, but it also highlights a recurring approach to James Gunn’s DC Universe that Lanterns showrunner Chris Mundy and his fellow executive producers Damon Lindelof and Tom King have taken. Namely, they talk a lot about all the aliens out there, but they really don’t show much of them at all. Let’s dig in a bit on all of this.

Does DC Comics Have a Planet of, Uh, Sentient Testicles?

Well, the answer to this one is… maybe kinda sorta? While we can take Hal at his word here that the movie/TV universe features a world where living, thinking, presumably talking balls exist, the comic books don’t quite go there.

That said, there is a race called the Noc'sagians (nut-sack-ians?) who could be said to look like testicles, albeit testicles with arms and legs and faces. One member of this race is a fellow named Galius Zed, who is actually the Green Lantern of his sector (Space Sector 1123 for those who are wondering). Then there’s also Zilius Zox, another Noc'sagian and a member of the mean old Red Lantern Corps. Guy Gardner – who’s played by Nathan Fillion in the DCU – has even been known to refer to Zox as a “testicle with teeth.” But in the nicest way possible!

Then looking to what is presumably a different live-action DC universe, the late, lamented Doom Patrol , which was also an HBO show (actually HBO Max after debuting on the also late DC Universe streaming service), featured a creature that’s come to be known as the Testicle Monster. While of unknown origin, the critter nonetheless plagued the non-heroes of that show in the final episode of its third season, “Amends Patrol.” “That's not a monster,” said Cliff Steele/Robotman. “That's a big nut sack with demon pubes.” Cannot deny.

How Many Alien Races Have Been Revealed in Lanterns?

Well, it’s hard to answer this one, but “a lot” is probably a fair statement, since the very existence of the Green Lantern Corps implies an untold number of alien worlds exist out in space. So putting aside the bigger DCU, which includes Kryptonians – of which we know there’s at least a man, a girl, and a dog – anyone revealed in Peacemaker Season 2 or Creature Commandos, and allllll the crazy aliens seen in the Supergirl movie, there have still been a bunch mentioned on Lanterns. But again, these various alien races are often discussed and rarely seen. Among them are:

The Guardians of the Universe (Laura Linney represent)

Manhunters (technically robots or androids, they are sentient and also from space so…)

The race that Antaan (Paul Ben-Victor) and his followers are members of

H'lvenites (the race that the squirrel-like Green Lantern Ch'p hails from)

Mogo (a living planet and a Green Lantern who “doesn’t socialize” according to Hal in Episode 2 – which is also a reference to an Alan Moore/Dave Gibbons GL story )

Bolovaxians (Green Lantern Kilowog’s race – we see a sketch of Kilowog in young John’s room)

Sentient testicles (actual name unknown!)

I might have missed some, so yell at me in the comments and let me know.

As for why we don’t get to see many actual aliens in Lanterns, the answer is pretty obvious. This show isn’t really about that stuff. Lanterns is about the uneasy alliance between Hal and John, and the manipulation that both have suffered by their parents (in John’s case, although Episode 4 seems to hint that maybe Hal has experienced some of this as well) and the Guardians. Yes, we get to briefly see Laura Linney’s Guardian Lianna in her alien form from behind, and Sinestro is here in all his pink glory, but generally the aliens on the show take human form to go undetected by those around them.

And no doubt to save on HBO’s budget too.

Talk to Scott Collura @scottcollura.bsky.social , or listen to his Star Trek podcast, Transporter Room 3 . Or do both!
